cards.text: Paul the apostle is finishing his letter to Timothy, the one he calls his beloved child (2 Timothy 1:2). Paul's in chains (2 Timothy 1:16), and he just said the time of his departure is at hand (2 Timothy 4:6). Now it gets personal, and Paul asks Timothy to make every effort to come to him quickly, which is apostle for DROP EVERYTHING.

cards.question: Paul wants Timothy there fast, because Demas, one of his fellow workers (Philemon 1:24), has deserted him and gone to Thessalonica. What pulled Demas away?

cards.text: Crescens has gone to Galatia, and Titus, Paul's partner and fellow worker (2 Corinthians 8:23), to Dalmatia. Paul's whole crew is scattering like a group chat where every ping is somebody leaving: ding, ding, DING.

cards.question: With Demas, Crescens and Titus gone, who is the only one still with Paul?
Paul tells Timothy to get Mark and bring him along. Why does Paul want Mark?

answers.text: He is useful in the ministry
He has money for the trip

cards.text: Back in Acts, Paul thought it best not to take Mark along, because Mark had deserted them in Pamphylia (Acts 15:38). Now Paul's asking for him by name, and friend, as a stamper who got called out of the back of a junk drawer, I LOVE a callback.

cards.question: Paul mentions Tychicus, a man he once sent to the Ephesians with news (Ephesians 6:21-22). True or false: like Demas, Tychicus has now deserted Paul.

cards.text: Then Paul gets practical: he left some things with a man named Carpus at Troas, and he wants Timothy to bring them when he comes. Friend, even an apostle has a list of stuff he left at somebody's house.

cards.question: When Timothy comes, Paul wants his ___ and his ___, especially the parchments.

cards.text: Then comes a name with a warning label on it: Alexander the coppersmith. Paul says Alexander did him great harm.

cards.question: Paul says the ___ will repay Alexander according to his deeds.
True or false: Paul tells Timothy that Alexander is no threat to him.

cards.text: Now Paul looks back at his first defense, his first time answering for himself. Picture him looking around the room for his people.

cards.question: At Paul's first defense, everyone ___ him, but the Lord ___ by him.
True or false: Paul wants the people who deserted him at his first defense to be charged for it.

cards.text: Everybody walked out on him, and Paul's response is: "May it not be charged against them." Friend, I've seen people hold a grudge longer over a parking spot.

cards.question: The Lord stood by Paul and strengthened him so the message would be fully proclaimed. Who would get to hear it?

cards.text: Then Paul says he was delivered from the mouth of the lion. Friend, my scariest moments were wondering if it was drawer cleanout day, and this man's talking about a LION'S MOUTH.

cards.question: Paul's already been rescued once. Looking ahead, what is he sure the Lord will do for him?

answers.text: Bring him safely into His heavenly kingdom
Set him free from his chains

cards.text: And Paul can't help himself: "To Him be the glory forever and ever. Amen." Friends gone, chains on, and he's STILL giving glory.

Then the greetings start: Paul says hello to Prisca and Aquila, the tentmaking couple he once worked with (Acts 18:2-3), and to the household of Onesiphorus. He adds that Erastus has remained at Corinth.

cards.question: Paul also mentions Trophimus, who once traveled with him (Acts 20:4). Why isn't Trophimus with Paul now?

answers.text: Paul left him sick in Miletus

cards.question: Paul makes that ask again, make every effort to come, and this time he adds a deadline. Timothy should come before ___.

cards.text: Then the greetings go the other way: Eubulus, Pudens, Linus, Claudia and all the brothers say hello to Timothy. It's the end-of-letter roll call, and EVERYBODY wants in.

cards.question: True or false: Paul ends the letter with one last warning about Alexander.

cards.text: Paul signs off: "The Lord be with your spirit. Grace be with you all." From a man in chains, the very last word is grace.

findings.problem: Verse 12 says Paul has sent Tychicus to Ephesus. That fact is never told. The true or false card only tells the baker that Tychicus did not desert Paul. No story card says where Tychicus went or that Paul sent him.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The fill in the blank asks the baker to guess the exact items Paul names (cloak and scrolls against tent, staff and sandals). It completes the wording of the line. It is the same kind of question as the Psalm 23 bad example about the oil.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: Calling Alexander 'a name with a warning label on it' gives away the answer to card 12. Card 12 asks whether Paul tells Timothy that Alexander is no threat. The answer is that Paul warns him to beware.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: Stop 1 ends on this true or false card. Two things in verse 15 are never told: Paul tells Timothy to beware of Alexander, and he gives the reason, that Alexander has vigorously opposed the message. The baker only learns that the statement was false.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The joke 'I've seen people hold a grudge longer over a parking spot' doesn't land. 'Longer' has nothing to compare against, because Paul holds no grudge at all. The comparison needs to be clear at once, for example people holding a grudge over something tiny.

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: The right answer 'Bring him safely into His heavenly kingdom' stands out. It is the longest answer, it has the only capitalized divine pronoun, and it is the only one in Bible phrasing. The wrong answers are plain and modern.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: Verse 18 also says the Lord will rescue Paul from every evil action. No card tells this. Only the heavenly kingdom half of the verse is covered.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: 'Paul can't help himself' states Paul's inner state as fact. It is not marked as Papa Dorin's own guess.

rule.text: He can guess at a feeling, marked as his own ("I think," "I bet"). Never as fact.

findings.problem: The true or false card asks about something that does not happen in the passage: a final warning about Alexander. It does not move the passage forward or test a detail the baker needs. The actual content of verse 22 is only told on the next story card.

rule.text: Ask about the moments that move the passage forward and the details the baker needs to understand it.

findings.problem: 'The very last word is grace' is not literally true. The letter's last word in the BSB is 'all' ("Grace be with you all."). It should say grace is the last thing Paul leaves them with, or something similar.

rule.text: What he points out must be true.

findings.problem: Several people are never introduced when they first show up, even though Scripture says who they are. Luke is the answer on stop 1 card 4 and is never identified (Colossians 4:14). Onesiphorus on stop 2 card 9 is described earlier in this same letter (2 Timothy 1:16-18). Erastus on stop 2 card 9 was one of Paul's helpers (Acts 19:22).

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."
